clue.text: Item supplied from dock?

definitions.meaning: an item is a single particular or point in a list
to dock an animal is to cut off its tail

explanation.definitionFit: A particular point is a small piece of a larger account, and docking cuts the tail away, hence the playful de-tail reading.

clue.text: Sound position to be in?

parts.note: the place you need to be within to catch a noise, the range over which a voice can be heard

explanation.definitionFit: The range within which something can be heard is exactly where you must be positioned to catch a sound.

clue.text: Adviser accepted plan for the most part

indicators.note: most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme
A is an abbreviation for accepted, as marked on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: An adviser has had a proposal largely approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts the last letter from IDEA, leaving IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant or counsellor to someone senior, a synonym for an adviser.

clue.text: Item of furniture one can squeeze in?

definitions.text: Item of furniture one can squeeze in?

parts.words: Item of furniture one can squeeze in?
parts.note: a small sofa for two where a couple can sit close and squeeze each other affectionately

explanation.definitionFit: A two-seater sofa for couples, so it is furniture where you squeeze up together, or squeeze your sweetheart.

clue.text: Petty Officer's given promotion and a pension

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Petty Officer, with the possessive S
an ad is an advertisement, a piece of promotion

explanation.surface: A naval rating gets advanced in rank and a retirement income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pension' here is the European sense of a boarding house, not a retirement payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is a Spanish inn, and a pension in the continental sense is a guest house or small hotel.

clue.text: Wrong to put in standard post

indicators.note: says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
ill as a noun means harm or wrong

explanation.surface: It is unjust to plant a flagpole with a banner on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright column, the same sort of thing as a post.

clue.text: Begging society to be flexible about raise

parts.note: to raise is to put up, giving the word up
pliant means flexible or bendy

explanation.surface: A club pleading with members to be open-minded over a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' links the flexible word to the raise rather than marking a container; the three pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant person entreats humbly, so the adjective means pleading or begging.

clue.text: Daily run's abandoned, so ring round

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them on the phone

indicators.note: wild and uninhibited, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word run, its possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A daily jog has been given up, so someone phones about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run's' looks like a jogger's outing, but RUN is only fodder; the urn is a vessel the dial goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal means happening each day or in the daytime, a formal word for daily.

clue.text: Challenged corrupt adventurer

parts.note: dared means challenged someone to do something
evil means wicked or corrupt

explanation.surface: Someone dared a crooked explorer to take on a task.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless thrill-seeker, someone who takes on risky adventures.

clue.text: Say no to draft policy

parts.note: to draw up is to draft, so draw means draft
the line is the official policy, as in toeing the party line

explanation.surface: Refuse to sign up for a conscription scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draft' looks like military conscription but means to draw up.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a firm limit beyond which you will not go is to refuse, an idiom for saying no.

clue.text: Reportedly the best level

indicators.note: signals the word for the best is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: a plum job is the best and most desirable one

explanation.surface: Rumour has it the finest standard has been reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb means true or exactly straight, so it can stand for level in the sense of accurate.

clue.text: Looks to go off and get some rest

parts.note: good looks are beauty
to go off is to drop off to sleep

explanation.surface: A model's appearance may fade, so she takes a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' suggests going bad, but here it is nodding off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a humorous idiom for a refreshing nap or an early night, supposedly good for the complexion.

clue.text: Pain unit in hospital receiving honour

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other

parts.note: A and E is the Accident and Emergency department of a British hospital
CH is Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: A sore patient on a ward is given an award.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital casualty department; CH is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: One's lilac is replaced by a shrub

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a different order

parts.note: the words one's, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone's lilac bush is swapped for another plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is replaced' rearranges ONESLILAC into ESCALLONI, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Escallonia is a genus of evergreen flowering bushes, often grown as garden hedging.

clue.text: Class hearing about flying out

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in court

indicators.note: letters in flight are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lesson on air travel being cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying out' suggests air travel, but 'flying' is the anagram signal working on the word out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching session with a small group, a kind of class.

clue.text: Meat's English, best for a stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook into a mixed-up state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe claims English beef is the finest cut for a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is a cooked joint, a traditional British meat dish.

clue.text: Assign duty to American in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back, so the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or duty

explanation.surface: Retrospectively placing a tax on a US citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or allocate a share, a synonym for assign.

clue.text: Number on courses given a date to enter, currently

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next
the pair goes inside the other word

parts.note: ways are paths or courses

explanation.surface: A diner is given a date to start several courses at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given ... to enter' puts AD inside WAYS, after its W.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means at the present time, a synonym for currently.

clue.text: Run further

definitions.meaning: in cricket an ... is a run not scored off the bat

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket run from a wide or bye is called this, and as an adjective it means additional.

clue.text: Go round carrying a doctor's old instrument

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: to tour is to go round
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic's ancient device is taken on a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambour is a drum, an old percussion instrument.

clue.text: Filling second volume first

indicators.note: says the volume word comes ahead of the other

parts.note: content is volume or capacity, as in cubic content

explanation.surface: A dentist does a second filling before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'second, volume first': the S comes second, CONTENT first.
explanation.definitionFit: The contents of a pie or container are what fills it, a noun sense of filling.

clue.text: Young, new leader on the rise

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word leads it

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb

explanation.surface: A youthful new party leader whose career is climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, so newly born or young.

clue.text: Quick reminder

definitions.meaning: a cue given to someone who forgets their lines

explanation.definitionFit: Prompt is an adjective for immediate and a noun for a theatre cue that jogs memory.

clue.text: Imam later perhaps linked to Institute? That's not important

indicators.note: suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A religious leader may later join a college, but that hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Immaterial means irrelevant, of no consequence.

clue.text: Small area of land in Pwllheli's leased

indicators.note: the letters are found within the following words

explanation.surface: A small plot of ground in a Welsh seaside town is rented out.
explanation.walkthrough: Pwllheli is a seaside town in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, often a small one surrounded by water.

clue.text: Was sorry to be pronounced vulgar

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and spelt a different way

parts.note: rude means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: Someone regretted being declared crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Rued is the past tense of rue, to regret, so it means felt sorry.

clue.text: Call up girl who's keeping fine

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Phoning a woman who is well.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory is to summon it to mind, an idiomatic sense of call up.

clue.text: Verify dimensions reach the required standard

definitions.meaning: to check the size of something with a tape or ruler
to be good enough, to meet expectations

explanation.definitionFit: Literally taking sizes, and idiomatically being adequate to a test or expectation.

clue.text: Paymaster tailor

parts.note: a pro is an expert or master of a craft
to tailor is to adapt or fit

explanation.surface: A man in charge of salaries who makes clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is gain or return, the reward one earns, so a kind of pay.

clue.text: Drug seen as cool

definitions.meaning: to drug someone is to calm them with a tranquilliser

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to tranquillise, and as an adjective calm and composed.
